Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Compiled scenarios**: the scripts listed in `!scnlist.txt` are compiled by `SceneParser.tjs` and played by the scene player (`KAGEnvPlayer.tjs`) however the game goes to them: a jump, a choice, `kag.process()` or a load. The sample's demo menu and demos play compiled (`doc/scn.txt`)
- **Going back** in compiled scenes: a BACK button in the message window, and a mark beside each message in the backlog, go back to that message with the World, the game's flags and KAG's own layers as they were
- **Scene replay and dialogue search**: the Replay screen has a tile for every titled scene, with a picture of it; a new Search screen in Extras finds the lines read so far by a word or a speaker and plays from the one chosen
- **kagex-release compiles a release's scenarios** (to `.scn` files) and leaves the scripts out, and **compiles every `.tjs` to TJS bytecode**, so a package carries no readable scripts
- **Signed game files**: kagex-release can sign a release, and the Windows, Linux, Steam and macOS builds check the game archive, the engine, its plugins and every patch before the game starts (the `sigcheck` plugin, in these packages). A changed, missing or differently signed file stops the game
- **One keys file**: the archive, scenario and signing keys, a key of its own for each, in one file kept outside the game. *Create keys…* in kagex-release's window or `kagex-release --cli keygen <file>` makes it
- **Encrypted archives and scenarios**: kagex-release encrypts `data.xp3` ([xp3crypt](https://github.com/krkren/xp3crypt)), optionally with the file names hidden too, and the compiled scenarios ([scnfile](https://github.com/krkren/scnfile)), and writes the keys into each build's engine. Every engine in this release, on every platform, has xp3crypt built in and the scnfile plugin
- kagex-release 0.9.0 downloads the 0.9.0 engines, and uses engine packages of your own from an `engines/` folder next to the game's `data/`

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.9.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
